entries.originalText: That seemeth a hard saying to many, If any man will come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his Cross and follow Me.(1) But it will be much harder to hear that last sentence, Depart from me, ye wicked, into eternal fire.(2) For they who now willingly hear the word of the Cross and follow it, shall not then fear the hearing of eternal damnation.
entries.modernizedText: That seems a hard saying to many, If anyone will come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his Cross and follow Me.(1) But it will be much harder to hear that last sentence, Depart from me, you wicked, into eternal fire.(2) For those who now willingly hear the word of the Cross and follow it will not then fear hearing eternal damnation.

entries.originalText: This sign of the Cross shall be in heaven when the Lord cometh to Judgment.
entries.modernizedText: This sign of the Cross will be in heaven when the Lord comes to Judgment.

entries.originalText: Then all servants of the Cross, who in life have conformed themselves to the Crucified, shall draw nigh unto Christ the Judge with great boldness.
entries.modernizedText: Then all servants of the Cross who in life have conformed themselves to the Crucified will draw near to Christ the Judge with great boldness.

entries.originalText: Why fearest thou then to take up the cross which leadeth to a kingdom?
entries.modernizedText: Why then do you fear to take up the cross that leads to a kingdom?

entries.originalText: In the Cross is health, in the Cross is life, in the Cross is protection from enemies, in the Cross is heavenly sweetness, in the Cross strength of mind, in the Cross joy of the spirit, in the Cross the height of virtue, in the Cross perfection of holiness.
entries.modernizedText: In the Cross is health, in the Cross is life, in the Cross is protection from enemies, in the Cross is heavenly sweetness, in the Cross strength of mind, in the Cross joy of the spirit, in the Cross the height of virtue, in the Cross perfection of holiness.

entries.originalText: There is no health of the soul, no hope of eternal life, save in the Cross.
entries.modernizedText: There is no health of the soul, no hope of eternal life, except in the Cross.

entries.originalText: Take up therefore, thy cross and follow Jesus and thou shalt go into eternal life.
entries.modernizedText: Take up your cross, therefore, and follow Jesus, and you will go into eternal life.

entries.originalText: He went before thee bearing His Cross and died for thee upon the Cross, that thou also mayest bear thy cross and mayest love to be crucified upon it.
entries.modernizedText: He went before you bearing His Cross and died for you upon the Cross, so that you also may bear your cross and love to be crucified upon it.

entries.originalText: For if thou be dead with Him, thou shalt also live with Him, and if thou be a partaker of His sufferings thou shalt be also of His glory.
entries.modernizedText: For if you are dead with Him, you will also live with Him, and if you share in His sufferings you will also share in His glory.

entries.originalText: Behold everything dependeth upon the Cross, and everything lieth in dying; and there is none other way unto life and to true inward peace, except the way of the Holy Cross and of daily mortification.
entries.modernizedText: Behold, everything depends upon the Cross, and everything lies in dying; and there is no other way to life and true inward peace except the way of the Holy Cross and of daily mortification.

entries.originalText: Go where thou wilt, seek whatsoever thou wilt, and thou shalt find no higher way above nor safer way below, than the way of the Holy Cross.
entries.modernizedText: Go where you will, seek whatever you will, and you will find no higher way above or safer way below than the way of the Holy Cross.

entries.originalText: Dispose and order all things according to thine own will and judgment, and thou shalt ever find something to suffer either willingly or unwillingly, and thus thou shalt ever find thy cross.
entries.modernizedText: Dispose and order all things according to your own will and judgment, and you will always find something to suffer either willingly or unwillingly, and thus you will always find your cross.

entries.originalText: For thou shalt either feel pain of body, or tribulation of spirit within thy soul.
entries.modernizedText: For you will feel either pain of body or tribulation of spirit within your soul.

entries.originalText: Sometimes thou wilt be forsaken of God, sometimes thou wilt be tried by thy neighbour, and which is more, thou wilt often be wearisome to thyself.
entries.modernizedText: Sometimes you will be forsaken by God, sometimes you will be tried by your neighbor, and what is more, you will often be wearisome to yourself.

entries.originalText: And still thou canst not be delivered nor eased by any remedy or consolation, but must bear so long as God will.
entries.modernizedText: And still you cannot be delivered or eased by any remedy or consolation, but must bear it as long as God wills.

entries.originalText: For God will have thee learn to suffer tribulation without consolation, and to submit thyself fully to it, and by tribulation be made more humble.
entries.modernizedText: For God would have you learn to suffer tribulation without consolation, submit yourself fully to it, and be made more humble by tribulation.

entries.originalText: No man understandeth the Passion of Christ in his heart so well as he who hath had somewhat of the like suffering himself.
entries.modernizedText: No one understands the Passion of Christ in his heart so well as the person who has himself had some similar suffering.

entries.originalText: The Cross therefore is always ready, and every where waiteth for thee.
entries.modernizedText: The Cross, therefore, is always ready and waits for you everywhere.

entries.originalText: Thou canst not flee from it whithersoever thou hurriest, for whithersoever thou comest, thou bearest thyself with thee, and shalt ever find thyself.
entries.modernizedText: You cannot flee from it wherever you hurry, for wherever you come, you carry yourself with you and will always find yourself.

entries.originalText: Turn thee above, turn thee below, turn thee without, turn thee within, and in them all thou shalt find the Cross; and needful is it that thou everywhere possess patience if thou wilt have internal peace and gain the everlasting crown.
entries.modernizedText: Turn above, turn below, turn outward, turn inward, and in them all you will find the Cross; and you must possess patience everywhere if you want inward peace and wish to gain the everlasting crown.

entries.originalText: If thou willingly bear the Cross, it will bear thee, and will bring thee to the end which thou seekest, even where there shall be the end of suffering; though it shall not be here.
entries.modernizedText: If you willingly bear the Cross, it will bear you and bring you to the end you seek, even where there will be an end to suffering, though it will not be here.

entries.originalText: If thou bear it unwillingly, thou makest a burden for thyself and greatly increaseth thy load, and yet thou must bear it.
entries.modernizedText: If you bear it unwillingly, you make a burden for yourself and greatly increase your load, and yet you must bear it.

entries.originalText: If thou cast away one cross, without doubt thou shalt find another and perchance a heavier.
entries.modernizedText: If you cast away one cross, without doubt you will find another and perhaps a heavier one.

entries.originalText: Thinketh thou to escape what no mortal hath been able to avoid?
entries.modernizedText: Do you think to escape what no mortal has been able to avoid?

entries.originalText: Which of the saints in the world hath been without the cross and tribulation?
entries.modernizedText: Which of the saints in the world has been without the cross and tribulation?

entries.originalText: For not even Jesus Christ our Lord was one hour without the anguish of His Passion, so long as He lived.
entries.modernizedText: For not even Jesus Christ our Lord was one hour without the anguish of His Passion as long as He lived.

entries.originalText: It behooved, He said, Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and so enter into his glory.(3) And how dost thou seek another way than this royal way, which is the way of the Holy Cross?
entries.modernizedText: It was necessary, He said, for Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and so enter into his glory.(3) And how do you seek another way than this royal way, which is the way of the Holy Cross?

entries.originalText: The whole life of Christ was a cross and martyrdom, and dost thou seek for thyself rest and joy?
entries.modernizedText: The whole life of Christ was a cross and martyrdom, and do you seek rest and joy for yourself?

entries.originalText: Thou art wrong, thou art wrong, if thou seekest aught but to suffer tribulations, for this whole mortal life is full of miseries, and set round with crosses.
entries.modernizedText: You are wrong, you are wrong if you seek anything but to suffer tribulations, for this whole mortal life is full of miseries and surrounded by crosses.

entries.originalText: And the higher a man hath advanced in the spirit, the heavier crosses he will often find, because the sorrow of his banishment increaseth with the strength of his love.
entries.modernizedText: And the higher a person has advanced in the spirit, the heavier the crosses he will often find, because the sorrow of his banishment increases with the strength of his love.

entries.originalText: But yet the man who is thus in so many wise afflicted, is not without refreshment of consolation, because he feeleth abundant fruit to be growing within him out of the bearing of his cross.
entries.modernizedText: But the person who is thus afflicted in so many ways is not without the refreshment of consolation, because he feels abundant fruit growing within him from bearing his cross.

entries.originalText: For whilst he willingly submitteth himself to it, every burden of tribulation is turned into an assurance of divine comfort, and the more the flesh is wasted by affliction, the more is the spirit strengthened mightily by inward grace.
entries.modernizedText: For while he willingly submits himself to it, every burden of tribulation is turned into an assurance of divine comfort, and the more the flesh is wasted by affliction, the more the spirit is mightily strengthened by inward grace.

entries.originalText: And ofttimes so greatly is he comforted by the desire for tribulation and adversity, through love of conformity to the Cross of Christ, that he would not be without sorrow and tribulation; for he believeth that he shall be the more acceptable to God, the more and the heavier burdens he is able to bear for His sake.
entries.modernizedText: And often he is so greatly comforted by the desire for tribulation and adversity, through love of conformity to the Cross of Christ, that he would not be without sorrow and tribulation; for he believes that the more and heavier burdens he is able to bear for God’s sake, the more acceptable he will be to Him.

entries.originalText: This is not the virtue of man, but the grace of Christ which hath such power and energy in the weak flesh, that what it naturally hateth and fleeth from, this it draweth to and loveth through fervour of spirit.
entries.modernizedText: This is not human virtue, but the grace of Christ, which has such power and energy in weak flesh that what it naturally hates and flees from, it draws toward and loves through fervor of spirit.

entries.originalText: It is not in the nature of man to bear the cross, to love the cross, to keep under the body and to bring it into subjection, to fly from honours, to bear reproaches meekly, to despise self and desire to be despised, to bear all adversities and losses, and to desire no prosperity in this world.
entries.modernizedText: It is not in human nature to bear the cross, to love the cross, to keep the body under control and bring it into subjection, to flee from honors, to bear reproaches meekly, to despise self and desire to be despised, to bear all adversities and losses, and to desire no prosperity in this world.

entries.originalText: If thou lookest to thyself, thou wilt of thyself be able to do none of this; but if thou trustest in the Lord, endurance shall be given thee from heaven, and the world and the flesh shall be made subject to thy command.
entries.modernizedText: If you look to yourself, you will by yourself be able to do none of this; but if you trust in the Lord, endurance will be given you from heaven, and the world and the flesh will be made subject to your command.

entries.originalText: Yea, thou shalt not even fear thine adversary the devil, if thou be armed with faith and signed with the Cross of Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Indeed, you will not even fear your adversary the devil if you are armed with faith and signed with the Cross of Christ.

entries.originalText: Set thyself, therefore, like a good and faithful servant of Christ, to the manful bearing of the Cross of thy Lord, who out of love was crucified for thee.
entries.modernizedText: Set yourself, therefore, like a good and faithful servant of Christ, to the courageous bearing of the Cross of your Lord, who out of love was crucified for you.

entries.originalText: Prepare thyself for the bearing many adversities and manifold troubles in this wretched life; because so it shall be with thee wheresoever thou art, and so in very deed thou shalt find it, wherever thou hide thyself.
entries.modernizedText: Prepare yourself to bear many adversities and manifold troubles in this wretched life, because so it will be with you wherever you are, and so you will indeed find it wherever you hide yourself.

entries.originalText: This it must be; and there is no means of escaping from tribulation and sorrow, except to bear them patiently.
entries.modernizedText: This must be so, and there is no means of escaping tribulation and sorrow except to bear them patiently.

entries.originalText: Drink thou lovingly thy Lord’s cup if thou desirest to be His friend and to have thy lot with Him.
entries.modernizedText: Drink your Lord’s cup lovingly if you desire to be His friend and have your lot with Him.

entries.originalText: Leave consolations to God, let Him do as seemeth best to Him concerning them.
entries.modernizedText: Leave consolations to God; let Him do as seems best to Him concerning them.

entries.originalText: But do thou set thyself to endure tribulations, and reckon them the best consolations; for the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us,(4) nor would they be even if thou wert to endure them all.
entries.modernizedText: But set yourself to endure tribulations and count them the best consolations; for the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that will be revealed in us,(4) nor would they be even if you were to endure them all.

entries.originalText: When thou hast come to this, that tribulation is sweet and pleasant to thee for Christ’s sake, then reckon that it is well with thee, because thou hast found paradise on earth.
entries.modernizedText: When you have come to the point that tribulation is sweet and pleasant to you for Christ’s sake, then consider that it is well with you, because you have found paradise on earth.

entries.originalText: So long as it is hard to thee to suffer and thou desirest to escape, so long it will not be well with thee, and tribulations will follow thee everywhere.
entries.modernizedText: As long as it is hard for you to suffer and you desire to escape, it will not be well with you, and tribulations will follow you everywhere.

entries.originalText: If thou settest thyself to that thou oughtest, namely, to suffer and to die, it shall soon go better with thee, and thou shalt find peace.
entries.modernizedText: If you set yourself to what you ought, namely, to suffer and to die, it will soon go better with you, and you will find peace.

entries.originalText: Though thou shouldest be caught up with Paul unto the third heaven,(5) thou art not on that account secure from suffering evil.
entries.modernizedText: Though you should be caught up with Paul to the third heaven,(5) you are not on that account secure from suffering evil.

entries.originalText: I will show him, saith Jesus, what great things he must suffer for My Name’s sake.(6) It remaineth, therefore, to thee to suffer, if thou wilt love Jesus and serve Him continually.
entries.modernizedText: I will show him, says Jesus, what great things he must suffer for My Name’s sake.(6) It remains for you, therefore, to suffer if you want to love Jesus and serve Him continually.

entries.originalText: Oh that thou wert worthy to suffer something for the name of Jesus, how great glory should await thee, what rejoicing among all the saints of God, what bright example also to thy neighbour!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, if you were worthy to suffer something for the name of Jesus, how great a glory would await you, what rejoicing among all the saints of God, what a bright example also to your neighbor!

entries.originalText: For all men commend patience, although few be willing to practise it.
entries.modernizedText: For everyone commends patience, although few are willing to practice it.

entries.originalText: Thou oughtest surely to suffer a little for Christ when many suffer heavier things for the world.
entries.modernizedText: Surely you ought to suffer a little for Christ when many suffer heavier things for the world.

entries.originalText: Know thou of a surety that thou oughtest to lead the life of a dying man.
entries.modernizedText: Know for certain that you ought to lead the life of a dying person.

entries.originalText: And the more a man dieth to himself, the more he beginneth to live towards God.
entries.modernizedText: And the more a person dies to himself, the more he begins to live toward God.

entries.originalText: None is fit for the understanding of heavenly things, unless he hath submitted himself to bearing adversities for Christ.
entries.modernizedText: No one is fit to understand heavenly things unless he has submitted himself to bearing adversities for Christ.

entries.originalText: Nothing more acceptable to God, nothing more healthful for thyself in this world, than to suffer willingly for Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Nothing is more acceptable to God, nothing more healthful for yourself in this world, than to suffer willingly for Christ.

entries.originalText: And if it were thine to choose, thou oughtest rather to wish to suffer adversities for Christ, than to be refreshed with manifold consolations, for thou wouldest be more like Christ and more conformed to all saints.
entries.modernizedText: And if it were yours to choose, you ought rather to wish to suffer adversities for Christ than to be refreshed with manifold consolations, for you would be more like Christ and more conformed to all saints.

entries.originalText: For our worthiness and growth in grace lieth not in many delights and consolations, but rather in bearing many troubles and adversities.
entries.modernizedText: For our worthiness and growth in grace lie not in many delights and consolations, but rather in bearing many troubles and adversities.

entries.originalText: If indeed there had been anything better and more profitable to the health of men than to suffer, Christ would surely have shown it by word and example.
entries.modernizedText: If indeed there had been anything better and more profitable to the health of people than to suffer, Christ would surely have shown it by word and example.

entries.originalText: For both the disciples who followed Him, and all who desire to follow Him, He plainly exhorteth to bear their cross, and saith, If any man will come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross, and follow Me.(7) So now that we have thoroughly read and studied all things, let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter.
entries.modernizedText: For He plainly exhorts both the disciples who followed Him and all who desire to follow Him to bear their cross, and says, If anyone will come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross, and follow Me.(7) So now that we have thoroughly read and studied all things, let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter.

entries.originalText: We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.(8)
entries.modernizedText: We must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.(8)
